title: The multiplication table problem in large dimensions
summary: For $N\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$, let $M_k(N):=\#\{x_1\cdots x_k : x_i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\text{ for all } i\}$ be the $k$-dimensional multiplication table. Given $N$, Khovanskii's theorem implies that $M_k(N)$ agrees, for all sufficiently large $k$, with a polynomial in $k$ of degree $π(N)$. We determine the asymptotic size of its leading coefficient, proving that, as $N\to\infty$, with $k$ sufficiently large relative to $N$, \[ M_k(N) = \exp\bigg((2π+o(1))\frac{\sqrt{N}}{\log N}\bigg)\frac{k^{π(N)}}{π(N)!}. \] We also study the analogous problem when the factors are restricted to $y$-smooth…
